steps.caption: The server runs quietly on an unpatched CMS. No alerts are firing; dashboards are green. Evidence: vulnerability scan report
steps.defender: a monthly vulnerability scan flagged the CMS version last month and the ticket is still open - the entry point was already known.

steps.title: 2 · Webshell established
steps.caption: The attacker probes the CMS upload endpoint. The WAF blocks twelve attempts, and one request evades a rule gap; a small webshell is now running on the server (shown conceptually - no exploit content). Evidence: WAF log
steps.defender: the WAF log shows 13 probes from one IP, 12 blocked, 1 allowed - and nobody has reviewed the allowed line.

steps.title: 3 · Harvesting text
steps.caption: Using the webshell, the attacker runs a database dump: the DB config file and the user table, stitched into one text blob and base64-encoded so it survives any input filtering. mysqldump spawned by the PHP worker user writing to a temp file - an odd parent process at an odd hour. Evidence: mysqldump process event

steps.title: 4 · One small POST
steps.caption: The server itself makes a quiet HTTPS POST to a paste-site API. The request is under a kilobyte: a fake dev key placeholder and the base64 blob as a form field. from a server subnet - servers never browse, so this single row justifies pulling the packet. Evidence: proxy POST row
steps.defender: the proxy logs a POST to a paste category

steps.caption: The paste service answers with a short URL, https://pastebin.com/abcd1234 in this example. The attacker now holds a public link to the stolen text. Evidence: paste URL in egress log
steps.defender: almost nothing - a 21-byte response archived in the egress log, easy to miss next to normal traffic.

steps.title: 6 · Attacker fetches raw
steps.caption: From his own infrastructure the attacker opens the raw paste to confirm the payload arrived intact. Evidence: brand-monitoring alert (external, later)
steps.defender: the SOC cannot see paste-site visitor analytics; the fetch itself is invisible. The dump usually surfaces later through brand monitoring or an external tip.

steps.title: 8 · SOC connects
steps.caption: The analyst joins the pieces - mysqldump, the paste POST, the login anomaly - and declares an incident. Paste categories are blocked for server ranges and an egress policy per asset class is created. Evidence: egress policy
steps.defender: the chain is cut at the egress point; future dumps from any server now fail closed.
